note.title: Spectral norm
note.desc: Spectral characterization of Sobolev norms: on compact manifolds, via Laplacian eigenfunctions. Proof via functional calculus and elliptic regularity, with explicit H¹ calculation.

3-equivalence-of-1-deltak2-graph-norm-an.text: 3. Equivalence of $(1-\Delta)^{k/2}$-graph norm and the usual Sobolev $H^k$ norm

pageProps.body:
Spectral norm

1. The H1H^1H1 calculation (concrete)

Let {φj}j≥0\{\varphi_j\}_{j\ge0}{φj​}j≥0​​ be an orthonormal L2L^2L2-basis of eigenfunctions of −Δ-\Delta−Δ with eigenvalues λj≥0\lambda_j\ge0λj​≥0:

−Δφj=λjφj,⟨φj,φℓ⟩L2=δjℓ.-\Delta\varphi_j=\lambda_j\varphi_j,\qquad\langle\varphi_j,\varphi_\ell\rangle_{L^2}=\delta_{j\ell}.−Δφj​=λj​φj​,⟨φj​,φℓ​⟩L2​=δjℓ​.

Expand w=∑jwjφjw=\sum_j w_j\varphi_jw=∑j​wj​φj​​ (convergence in L2L^2L2). Then

∥(1−Δ)1/2w∥L22=∑j(1+λj) ∣wj∣2,\|(1-\Delta)^{1/2}w\|_{L^2}^2 =\sum_j \big(1+\lambda_j\big)\,|w_j|^2,∥(1−Δ)1/2w∥L22​=∑j​(1+λj​)∣wj​∣2,

because (1−Δ)1/2φj=(1+λj)1/2φj(1-\Delta)^{1/2}\varphi_j=(1+\lambda_j)^{1/2}\varphi_j(1−Δ)1/2φj​=(1+λj​)1/2φj​​ and Parseval / Plancherel give the squared L2L^2L2-norm as the sum of squared coefficients.

So the spectral sum with weight (1+λj)(1+\lambda_j)(1+λj​) is exactly the squared L2L^2L2-norm of (1−Δ)1/2(1-\Delta)^{1/2}(1−Δ)1/2.

Now the usual Sobolev H1H^1H1 norm on a compact manifold is equivalent to the graph norm of (1−Δ)1/2(1-\Delta)^{1/2}(1−Δ)1/2; concretely there exist constants c,C>0c,C>0c,C>0 depending only on the manifold so that

c  ∥(1−Δ)1/2w∥L2≤∥w∥H1≤C  ∥(1−Δ)1/2w∥L2.c\;\|(1-\Delta)^{1/2}w\|_{L^2}\le \|w\|_{H^1}\le C\;\|(1-\Delta)^{1/2}w\|_{L^2}.c∥(1−Δ)1/2w∥L2​≤∥w∥H1​≤C∥(1−Δ)1/2w∥L2​.

Combining this with the identity above yields

∥w∥H12≃∑j(1+λj) ∣wj∣2,\|w\|_{H^1}^2 \simeq \sum_j (1+\lambda_j)\,|w_j|^2,∥w∥H12​≃∑j​(1+λj​)∣wj​∣2,

which is the H1H^1H1 instance of the claim.

(Why is the equivalence true? On a compact manifold ∥w∥H12\|w\|_{H^1}^2∥w∥H12​​ is ∥w∥L22+∥∇w∥L22\|w\|_{L^2}^2+\|\nabla w\|_{L^2}^2∥w∥L22​+∥∇w∥L22​​. Using the eigen-expansion one checks ∥∇w∥L22=∑jλj∣wj∣2\|\nabla w\|_{L^2}^2=\sum_j\lambda_j|w_j|^2∥∇w∥L22​=∑j​λj​∣wj​∣2. Hence ∥w∥H12=∑j(1+λj)∣wj∣2\|w\|_{H^1}^2=\sum_j(1+\lambda_j)|w_j|^2∥w∥H12​=∑j​(1+λj​)∣wj​∣2 up to the choice of normalization and conventions — so in fact for H1H^1H1 one often gets equality (no constants) when you identify norms appropriately.)

2. The general HkH^kHk (spectral functional calculus)

Exactly the same spectral computation works for any real k≥0k\ge0k≥0. By functional calculus

(1−Δ)k/2φj=(1+λj)k/2φj,(1-\Delta)^{k/2}\varphi_j=(1+\lambda_j)^{k/2}\varphi_j,(1−Δ)k/2φj​=(1+λj​)k/2φj​,

so for w=∑jwjφjw=\sum_j w_j\varphi_jw=∑j​wj​φj​,

∥(1−Δ)k/2w∥L22=∑j(1+λj)k∣wj∣2.\|(1-\Delta)^{k/2}w\|_{L^2}^2 =\sum_j (1+\lambda_j)^{k}|w_j|^2.∥(1−Δ)k/2w∥L22​=∑j​(1+λj​)k∣wj​∣2.

Thus the right-hand spectral sum is exactly the squared L2L^2L2-norm of (1−Δ)k/2w(1-\Delta)^{k/2}w(1−Δ)k/2w.

3. Equivalence of (1−Δ)k/2(1-\Delta)^{k/2}(1−Δ)k/2-graph norm and the usual Sobolev HkH^kHk norm

What remains is to explain why the graph norm ∥(1−Δ)k/2w∥L2\|(1-\Delta)^{k/2}w\|_{L^2}∥(1−Δ)k/2w∥L2​​ is equivalent to the standard Sobolev norm ∥w∥Hk\|w\|_{H^k}∥w∥Hk​​. On a compact manifold this is standard:

  • The operator 1−Δ1-\Delta1−Δ is a positive, elliptic, self-adjoint pseudodifferential operator of order 2. Its (fractional) powers (1−Δ)k/2(1-\Delta)^{k/2}(1−Δ)k/2 are elliptic pseudo-differential operators of order k.
  • Elliptic regularity (or basic pseudodifferential calculus) implies that the graph norm of any positive elliptic operator of order k is equivalent to the standard Sobolev HkH^kHk-norm. Concretely, there exist constants c,C>0c,C>0c,C>0 (dependent only on the geometry of SSS and kkk) such that for all w∈C∞(S)w\in C^\infty(S)w∈C∞(S), c  ∥(1−Δ)k/2w∥L2≤∥w∥Hk≤C  (∥w∥L2+∥(1−Δ)k/2w∥L2).c\;\|(1-\Delta)^{k/2}w\|_{L^2} \le \|w\|_{H^k} \le C\;\big(\|w\|_{L^2}+\|(1-\Delta)^{k/2}w\|_{L^2}\big).c∥(1−Δ)k/2w∥L2​≤∥w∥Hk​≤C(∥w∥L2​+∥(1−Δ)k/2w∥L2​). On a compact manifold the two-sided inequality can be tightened (by adjusting constants) to show full equivalence (no extra low-order term needed if you use (1−Δ)k/2(1-\Delta)^{k/2}(1−Δ)k/2 itself as the defining operator).

If you prefer an elementary (but longer) route: cover the manifold with finitely many coordinate charts, use a partition of unity, and compare the local Euclidean Sobolev norms defined by derivatives up to order k with the global spectral norm. The finiteness of the cover and standard elliptic estimates give the equivalence constants.

4. Conclusion

Putting items (2) and (3) together yields the desired equivalence:

∥w∥Hk2  ≃  ∑j≥0(1+λj)k ∣wj∣2,\|w\|_{H^k}^2 \;\simeq\; \sum_{j\ge0} (1+\lambda_j)^k\,|w_j|^2,∥w∥Hk2​≃∑j≥0​(1+λj​)k∣wj​∣2,

where the symbol ≃\simeq≃ means equality up to multiplicative constants depending only on kkk and the Riemannian manifold SSS.
